title: The normal quotient of a complete first-countable topological group is complete for its right uniformity
source_title: mathlib4: Uniform structure on topological groups
difficulty_reason: 商空间中的Cauchy序列不能通过任意选择代表元直接得到原群中的Cauchy序列；完备性也不是连续满射的一般保性。本组作者从商的Cauchy条件取得可随指定代表元校正另一个代表元的局部lift性质，递归选取足够稀疏的子序列，再逐步选择相邻商落入u(n+1)的相容代表元。关键是一般群的零邻域不必是子群：作者利用u(n+1)^2⊆u(n)作递减归纳，控制任意远的代表元之商，避免非交换误差随递归累计失控，由此产生一条真正Cauchy的lift并传回原商序列极限。这一代表元校正与非交换收缩邻域误差控制由602–680作者链实际承担，超过常规资格题的直接完备性保性/定义核对，判H2。Sigma类型和显式uniformity实例是实现表示，不作为难度依据；经典、命名、课本或文献已有地位均不作为排除条件。

comparisons.actual_assumptions_conclusion: R topological ring; M complete linearly topologized R-module with countable zero-neighbourhood basis; closed submodule N. Then M/N complete and M->M/N open.
comparisons.difference: The current theorem allows general noncommutative topological groups, arbitrary normal subgroups, and neighbourhoods not required to be subgroups. It asserts Cauchy completeness for the right uniformity without a T0/closedness hypothesis. The prior statement is a genuine overlapping linear-topology special case in its completeness component, rather than an identical claim.
comparisons.additional_load_bearing_obligation: Coherently choose lifts and control their finite noncommutative products using shrinking neighbourhoods u(n+1)^2⊆u(n), rather than rely on closure of products inside a fixed open submodule. This is explicitly performed at620–670, not hidden in a cited quotient-completeness theorem.
comparisons.counting_note: One candidate for the stated general-group theorem; record extension/overlap relation. No exhaustive equivalence certificate and no claim that mere title difference establishes uniqueness.

comparisons.actual_assumptions_conclusion: For an element of the free Boolean group on a pseudometric set with distinct support, its extended pseudometric norm has a minimizing pair representation, with even/odd support description.
comparisons.difference: A norm-minimizing finite support representation, not completeness of arbitrary normal quotient groups or Cauchy subsequence lifting.

comparisons.actual_assumptions_conclusion: There exist R complete with respect to principal I and principal J such that R/J is not I-adically complete.
comparisons.difference: An adic algebraic-completion counterexample is not the same assertion as right-uniform Cauchy completeness of a possibly nonseparated topological quotient. Do not identify these completion notions or add a closedness/T0 assumption to the author theorem; no proof-level resolution of the counterexample is claimed.

comparisons.actual_assumptions_conclusion: For a taut continuous homomorphism A->B of linearly topologized rings with dense image, complete countably based A and separated B, the map is open and surjective, B is complete and B=A/K for closed K.
comparisons.difference: Requires linear ring topology, tautness, dense image and a separated target; the current general-group quotient theorem has a specified normal quotient and uses an explicit Cauchy-lift construction. Related completeness mechanism, differing premises and result; not the same claim.
